consent.title: Before you use Development Mode
consent.intro: Development Mode lets a model change files in a managed worktree and runs your repository's own build, test and lint commands on this machine. Read this once before you start.
consent.container: On this node those commands run inside a container: read-only root filesystem, all capabilities dropped, no host namespaces, and only the managed worktree and runtime directories mounted.
consent.containerNetwork: Egress is denied for the sandbox the agent works in: the container provider can enforce it. Only the engine's own dependency restore, run against your base commit before the agent starts, is given the network.
consent.processUser: On this node those commands run as the signed-in user account that runs the engine — with that account's access to your files, not just the repository.
consent.processNetwork: Egress is denied for the sandbox the agent works in wherever this node can enforce it — Linux with a working sandbox network probe, or a container provider. Where it cannot, such as Windows, those commands reach the network unrestricted. Only the engine's own dependency restore, run against your base commit before the agent starts, is given the network. The Sandbox isolation panel reports which posture this node served.
consent.processLimits: CPU, memory and process-count ceilings are requested for these commands wherever this node can enforce them (the isolation panel shows whether it does): all logical cores, 75% of memory with a 4 GB floor, and 4096 processes by default, and an operator can override them. Where the host cannot impose them — Windows — no ceiling applies and a runaway command is bounded only by its timeout and the machine.
consent.trust: Register only repositories you trust. Repository code executes either way.

samplingOptions.title: Advanced sampling options
samplingOptions.description: These parameters override the model defaults for the next message send. They are stored in this browser only and are not persisted per-conversation.
samplingOptions.temperatureDescription: Controls randomness. Lower values are more deterministic; higher values are more creative.
samplingOptions.topPDescription: Nucleus sampling threshold. Only tokens whose cumulative probability reaches this value are considered.
samplingOptions.topKDescription: Limits sampling to the top K most likely tokens.
samplingOptions.minPDescription: Minimum probability for a token to be considered relative to the most probable token.
samplingOptions.repeatPenaltyDescription: Penalizes repetition. Values above 1 discourage the model from repeating itself.
samplingOptions.repeatLastNDescription: Number of tokens to look back when applying the repeat penalty. -1 uses the full context.
samplingOptions.presencePenaltyDescription: Penalizes tokens that have already appeared in the output, regardless of frequency.
samplingOptions.frequencyPenaltyDescription: Penalizes tokens proportionally to how often they have already appeared in the output.
samplingOptions.maxOutputTokensDescription: Maximum number of tokens to generate. Clamped to the model context length when set.
samplingOptions.seedDescription: Random seed for reproducibility. -1 uses a random seed.
samplingOptions.numCtxDescription: Size of the context window in tokens used to generate the next token. On the local llama.cpp runtime the server window is fixed when the model is loaded, so this only limits how much conversation history is sent.
samplingOptions.stopDescription: One stop sequence per line. The model halts when it emits any of these strings.
